title: Cash flow vs profit
summary: Operating cash flow is the cash the business actually collected. Free cash flow = operating cash flow − capital expenditure. Over time, cash should roughly follow profit.
unreliableWhen: In a single year, when a big order or a delayed payment shifts cash between years, or for a young company investing heavily on purpose.
goodExample: A fictional food maker's operating cash flow is above its net income every year, and free cash flow covers its dividend.
badExample: A fictional wholesaler reports rising profit while its operating cash flow falls almost to zero and it borrows to fill the gap.
